_doc: Trivy checks Hagstone hides by default (shown with --include-hardening): best-practice gaps that don't expose anything on their own. Every LOW check is hidden too. Each entry says why. A change must keep the IaC bench gate. See docs/specs/iac-containers-sbom.md.

hardening.AWS-0077: Backup retention is resilience, not exposure
hardening.AWS-0086: Missing S3 public access block: AWS blocks public access by default since April 2023; AWS-0092 reports a bucket that is actually public
hardening.AWS-0087: Missing S3 public access block (see AWS-0086)
hardening.AWS-0090: S3 versioning protects against accidental deletes; its absence exposes nothing
hardening.AWS-0091: Missing S3 public access block (see AWS-0086)
hardening.AWS-0093: Missing S3 public access block (see AWS-0086)
hardening.AWS-0132: Customer-managed KMS key instead of the AWS-managed one; data is encrypted either way
hardening.AWS-0176: IAM database authentication is an alternative to passwords, not a fix for an exposure
hardening.AWS-0177: Deletion protection is resilience, not exposure
hardening.KSV-0001: allowPrivilegeEscalation is defense in depth; KSV-0017 reports privileged containers
hardening.KSV-0013: Image tag :latest is a reproducibility issue, not an exposure
hardening.KSV-0014: Read-only root filesystem is defense in depth
hardening.KSV-0104: Seccomp profile is defense in depth
hardening.KSV-0118: Fires on any pod without an explicit securityContext; the specific checks (privileged, root, host access) carry the signal
hardening.KSV-0125: Trusted-registry allow-list is an organisation policy; Trivy's default list flags every private registry
